title: Pass-the-Hash
overview: Review an NTLM network logon on a host that typically receives traffic from managed services.
prerequisites: Know the basics of AD auditing and how to review authorization context.

attack.name: Pass the Hash
attack.rationale: An anomalous NTLM logon is compatible with pass-the-hash, but the authentication record does not identify credential form.

hypothesis: A successful NTLM network logon by a local administrator from a peer workstation warrants host-to-host review.
evidence: Check package, logon type, peer zone and account class. Correlate authentication and process activity on both systems.
false_positive: An approved help-desk task can use legacy authentication between systems.
tuning: Identify approved jump hosts and prefer central, constrained administration over broad user exclusions.
response: Scope the source and destination, preserve access logs, and reset impacted local administrator credentials if appropriate.
prevention: Roll out unique managed local administrator passwords, restrict NTLM and segment administration traffic.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: NTLM logon metadata alone cannot distinguish a password from another form of authentication material.

questions.explanation: Event 4624 establishes success and type 3 indicates a network logon.

options: Both source and destination endpoint activity
questions.explanation: A lateral movement assessment needs evidence across systems.
